newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan third-quarter GDP seen growing below target.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan third-quarter GDP seen growing below target.

text.p: Economists said on Monday they expected Taiwan's third-quarter gross domestic product growth to achieve a below-target 5.9-6.0 percent, saying investment recovery has been slowed by a crackdown on gang-linked business.
A survey of experts also noted that a slower-than-expected rebound in exports would contribute to a relatively lacklustre showing when the official GDP figures are reported on Friday.
Most said GDP growth, as measured by the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, was likely to undershoot the cabinet agency's most recent forecast of 6.09 percent.
"We did not see apparent recovery in both the public and private investments in the third quarter," said Wu Hui-lin, research fellow at Chunghua Institution for Economic Research.
Wu attributed the slow investment mainly to the government's aggressive drive to reduce the involvement of organised crime syndicates in public construction projects.
"Because of the crackdown, many investors have slowed their investment progress and some have temporarily stopped considering new investments," Wu said.
Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang said sluggish export growth was another factor undermining overall GDP growth, although a local consumer revival would limit the impact.
"Exports (in the quarter) did not show significant recovery," she said. "But private consumption should rise 6.3 percent year-on-year to sustain a 6.0 percent GDP growth in the third quarter."
Nomura projected full-year 1996 GDP growth at 5.8 percent, compared with Chunghua's 5.78 percent and the statistics directorate's August forecast of 5.89 percent.
Chunghua forecast third-quarter GDP at 5.92 percent.
But economists voiced optimism about the fourth-quarter, projecting GDP growth of 6.4 to 6.6 percent on the strength of stimulus measures promoted by President Lee Teng-hui.
"President Lee in June demanded that all government offices effectively boost...investment within six months and we see the positive results of this," Wu said.

The state has eased rules to promote Formosa Plastics group's US$9 billion petrochemical complex project and orchestrated a restoration of parliamentary support for the island's US$4.1 billion fourth nuclear power plant.
The finance ministry has completed tax-incentive proposals that are likely to encourage investments.

"The government has kept on offering various incentives or liberalising markets to attract foreign investors to set up regional operation centres in Taiwan, and that should gradually show more effect from the fourth quarter," Wu said.
Fourth-quarter private investment likely would jump 11.31 percent year-on-year, against just 6.69 percent in the third quarter, Wu said.

A stock market bull run that pushed the Taiwan index to a 1996 high of 6,659.72 points on Monday and a continued rise in private consumption should contribute to a better GDP showing in the fourth quarter, said Nomura's Huang.
"With the stock index hitting a new high and private consumption expected to do well in the hot-sale season in department stores, fourth-quarter GDP performance should be quite good," Huang said.
